scope: Adults with upper airway resistance syndrome, focused on definition and treatment evidence.

keyRecommendations.text: A single diagnostic criterion is still not defined; authors disagree on whether UARS is distinct from obstructive sleep apnoea.
Treatment studies have used heterogeneous thresholds, including AHI less than 5–15 events/hour and oesophageal pressure more negative than 10 or 20 mmHg.
Nasal CPAP has been the mainstay therapy but with limited effectiveness.

clinicalBottomLine: This review does not support a single PSG cut-off for UARS. CPAP is the usual prescription, with limited effectiveness, and oral-appliance efficacy is not yet established.
notableCaveats: The paper is a treatment-focused narrative review of heterogeneous studies, not a new diagnostic standard.
